name: Phone Eye-Roll
description: A phone with an eye-roll means the sender is annoyed at a device or at the person lighting it up. The texts are tedious, excessive, or badly timed. It is not a request for a call.
meaning: The eye-roll says "really?" and the phone says the "really" is about messages, notifications, or someone who will not stop writing. 📱🙄 vents about the inbox. It does not mean "please call me." A call request would not be rolling its eyes.
seoDescription: What does 📱🙄 mean? Annoyance at a phone: too many texts, a tedious thread, or notifications. It is not "please call."

longForm.overview:
An eye-roll is a short "really," and it can be playful or genuinely unimpressed depending on the friendship. A phone next to it names the object of the complaint. 📱🙄 means the device, or the person on the other end of it, is doing too much. Twelve messages from a boss. A group chat that will not sleep. A notification that buzzed through dinner. An app that wants a review at the worst moment. The sender is venting to someone who is not, they hope, the problem. If you are the person who sent the twelve messages, and you see this in a side chat, the joke is on you. Consider stopping.

It is the opposite of a request to talk. "Call me" emojis exist, and this is not their shape. Rolling your eyes at the phone means you want fewer rings, not another one. Parents send it about school apps. Friends send it about a thread they have muted and are still somehow reading. The playful version, between people who text constantly, means "we are like this and I am pretending to suffer." The serious version means a boundary is forming. Look at the count and the clock. "You texted 📱🙄" aimed at you, with a time attached, is a boundary. Laughing it off teaches them you did not hear it.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
📱🙄 is a reaction sent to a third person: a friend hears about the annoying thread, not the annoying sender. That triangulation is the point. They want a witness before they reply, or instead of replying.

It also captions screenshots. The screenshot is where the actual offense is. Do not ask "what happened" if the image is right there. Read it, then take their side unless the side is unfair and you are close enough to say so.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not send 📱🙄 as your reply to the person you are annoyed at, unless you want the conflict to be about your tone. Tell them the actual problem.

Do not use it to mock someone's access needs, a safety check-in, or a parent texting about a kid. Those messages are allowed to light up a phone. And do not send it in a work channel about a client by name. Screenshot vents leak.
longForm.howToReply:
If you are the witness, you can say "mute it" or "that is a lot" and stop. They may not want a strategy memo.

If you are the cause, send fewer messages and acknowledge the pile. A new pile of apologies is still a pile. If the eye-roll is playful and you both text like that, match it once and move on. Repeating the bit all day becomes the tedious thread.

faqs.question: What does 📱🙄 mean?
faqs.answer: 📱🙄 means the sender is annoyed at their phone or at whoever keeps lighting it up. Too many texts, bad timing, or a tedious notification.

faqs.question: Does 📱🙄 mean call me?
faqs.answer: No. An eye-roll at the phone is a complaint about contact, not a request for more. If they wanted a call, the face would not be rolling.

faqs.question: What if I am the one who texted too much?
faqs.answer: Ease off and say you saw it. Do not send a burst of "sorry" messages. The volume was the issue.

faqs.question: Is 📱🙄 always serious?
faqs.answer: No. Close friends use it as a playful complaint about a chat they like. A time, a count, or a "please stop" makes it a real boundary.

conversationExamples.message: he double texted and then triple texted 📱🙄
conversationExamples.interpretation: They want a witness, not necessarily advice. Agree it is a lot. Let them decide whether to reply.

conversationExamples.message: after-hours ping 📱🙄 I will answer tomorrow
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are setting a work boundary. Do not chase them tonight if you can avoid it.

conversationExamples.message: I like you and I also need fewer goodnights, 📱🙄 in a nice way
conversationExamples.interpretation: A real boundary wrapped in a joke. Cut the late messages. The affection is still there. The volume is the problem.

conversationExamples.message: the school app again 📱🙄 it is always the app
conversationExamples.interpretation: They are tired of institutional notifications. Sympathize. You probably cannot fix the app.

conversationExamples.message: muting the planning thread 📱🙄 tell me if the time actually changes
conversationExamples.interpretation: They want out of the chatter and in on the decision. Only ping them for the final plan.
